title: Implement HLG-1 as an additive versioned view over the existing graph
context: The Engineering Landscape and reciprocal ORC boundary are documented, but Hunch cannot yet persist or deliver versioned resource fragments. The next step must establish the durable schema without pulling runtime discovery or orchestration into Hunch.
decision: Implement HLG-1 first: add a versioned resource record and typed resource relationships as an additive view over the existing JSON-authoritative graph, with deterministic identities, lifecycle, credential-free locators, provenance, currentness, forward migration and rebuildable SQLite projections. Stop before deterministic discovery, cross-repository traversal or a new delivery surface.
consequences: Existing graph records must forward-migrate without loss before Zod validation
JSON remains the source of truth and SQLite remains derived
Resource and relationship identities must remain stable across reindex and clean clones
Secret-bearing locators or metadata are rejected before persistence or delivery
HLG-2 discovery and HLG-3 delivery build only after the HLG-1 contract is stable
alternatives_rejected: Create a separate landscape database or graph authority beside the existing graph — revisit if the current graph cannot represent typed resource relationships without breaking legacy records
Put live service, CLI or MCP health discovery into Hunch — revisit only if live state becomes durable and useful with every process stopped
Design an ORC-specific context envelope instead of reusing validated delivery — revisit only if the generic envelope cannot preserve fragment receipts
Start manifest discovery before the resource identity and migration contract is proven — revisit after HLG-1 acceptance

premises.claim: The reciprocal Engineering Landscape contract remains the approved Hunch/ORC ownership boundary
